change.describe: branch `pr-94942` of grafana-94942 against cbe1e7d63f098e306058c0fbcab2f5c30602fa7d (merge-base cbe1e7d)
change.title: pr-94942
change.author: Sam Jewell

findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and ignores the feature flag
findings.body: Both branches return false: `enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(...)`, and if it is true the function returns false, otherwise it returns false too. The flag is evaluated but has no effect, and the name `enabled` holds the inverse of the flag. The result is a hard-coded kill switch that reads like a flag check. If the goal is to disable SQL expressions unconditionally, drop the helper and return the error directly in `case QueryTypeSQL` with a comment saying it is disabled and why. If the flag should still gate the feature, the function should return `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`. As written, enabling `sqlExpressions` does nothing.

findings.title: Disabled SQL gives different errors on the two parse paths
findings.body: The reader path (`ReadQuery`) returns `sqlExpressions is not implemented`. The legacy path in `pkg/expr/nodes.go:159-160` calls `UnmarshalSQLCommand` directly with no flag check. That reaches `NewSQLCommand`, where `sql.TablesList` always fails against the stub DB (`pkg/expr/sql/db.go:12-14`). The user then gets the public message `error reading SQL command` (`pkg/expr/sql_command.go:33-35`), and the server logs a Warn that the SQL is invalid. The same query is therefore reported as a feature-disabled error on one path and as a SQL syntax error on the other, even when the SQL is valid. Add the disabled check in one place both paths share (for example at the top of `NewSQLCommand`) so users and logs see one consistent reason.

findings.title: Stub DB leaves most of the SQL expression code unreachable
findings.body: Every method returns `not implemented`. `TablesList` in `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go` therefore always fails at `RunCommands`, so `tablesFromAST` and the JSON/AST handling are unreachable. `SQLCommand.Execute` is never reached, because `NewSQLCommand` always errors. The tests in `pkg/expr/sql/parser_test.go` and `pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go` are already `t.Skip()`, so nothing in this PR exercises the stub. This is acceptable as a temporary disable. Add a comment on `DB` saying it is a placeholder that replaces go-duck and why, so a later reader does not take it for a real implementation. A named sentinel error such as `ErrNotImplemented` would also let callers tell this case apart from a real SQL error (see the reader.go finding).

contracts.action: A query of type `sql` is read through ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery
contracts.equivalent_path: Other query types in ReadQuery (math, reduce, etc.) build a Command from the parsed body; the `threshold` case gates a sub-feature on `h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagRecoveryThreshold)` at pkg/expr/reader.go:160.
contracts.before_after: Before: it parsed the body and built an SQLCommand, backed by go-duck. After: it returns `sqlExpressions is not implemented` before reading the body, whatever the flag value (reader.go:194-200 always returns false).
contracts.visible_effect: Any SQL expression read through this path fails with `sqlExpressions is not implemented`. The error is returned up the `nodes.go:137-143` caller.
contracts.failure_mode: Not silent: an explicit error is returned. The flag value is ignored, so enabling the toggle has no effect.

contracts.action: NewSQLCommand now calls sql.TablesList backed by the stub DB, and Execute calls the stub QueryFramesInto
contracts.equivalent_path: Same function as before, with duck.NewInMemoryDB replaced by sql.NewInMemoryDB (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:23). The legacy path nodes.go:159-160 calls UnmarshalSQLCommand with no feature check.
contracts.before_after: Before: TablesList parsed the SQL via DuckDB json_serialize_sql. After: RunCommands returns errors.New("not implemented") (db.go:16-18), so TablesList returns an error and NewSQLCommand returns BadRequest `sql-invalid-sql` with public message `error reading SQL command`. Execute is no longer reachable.
contracts.visible_effect: Legacy-path users who send a SQL expression get `failed to parse expression '<refId>': ... error reading SQL command`, which blames the SQL rather than the disabled feature.
contracts.failure_mode: The failure is visible, but its message is misleading. The server logs a Warn and an Error that include the raw user SQL on each attempt (parser.go:28, sql_command.go:32).

summary: The PR disables SQL expressions by removing go-duck and putting a stub DB in its place. That is consistent with the title, and nothing breaks at compile time that I can see. I found three problems, all minor. `enableSqlExpressions` returns false on every branch, so it looks like a flag check but never reads the flag. The reader path and the legacy `nodes.go` path report a disabled feature differently: one says `not implemented`, the other says `error reading SQL command`. The stub leaves the parser and `Execute` code unreachable and has no comment saying it is a placeholder. The go.mod, go.sum and go.work.sum edits are only removed or moved dependency lines. I did not build or run anything, so I could not check that the removed indirect dependencies are unused elsewhere.
